Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.

payload.instruction: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the transformed object retain its identity as a DVD?
node.criteria: Pass if the object remains identifiable as a DVD; fail if it is no longer identifiable as a DVD; unknown if its identity cannot be determined from the image.
node.binding: Assess whether the transformed object is still the DVD shown in the input image.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image shows a white circular disc with a central hole, consistent with a DVD, in the location of the dark disc-like object in the source. Its disc shape and center opening preserve its identity as a DVD.
The edited image shows a white circular disc with a central hole, consistent with a DVD, in the area where the black disc-like object appeared in the source. Its DVD identity remains recognizable.
The edited image shows a white circular optical disc with a central hole, retaining the recognizable form of a DVD. The source also contains a disc-like object in the corresponding area.
The edited image shows a white circular disc with a central hole, consistent with a DVD, in the area where the source image shows the DVD case/disc. Its DVD identity remains recognizable.

The edited image shows a white circular disc with a central hole in the area where the black DVD was, retaining the recognizable form of a DVD. The source also shows a disc-like object in that location.

response.content: {"text":"The binding asks only whether the object remains a DVD, so it rewards recognizable disc shape and misses whether the requested edit was actually applied to the source DVD. In the images, the source DVD is the small square case near the center; the black object to its right appears to be a separate animal, not the DVD. The edited image removes the case and shows two white discs, while the animal remains. Refine this node’s binding/criterion to compare the source DVD’s location and identity across snapshots and assess the requested transformation on that object, rather than treating any nearby white disc as proof of success. Preserve an unresolved outcome when correspondence is uncertain; do not infer completion from color or shape alone. The five consistent high-confidence passes indicate a systematic binding/evidence error, not transport or dependency failure. The aggregate ‘no’ is a constraint on the overall edit judgment, not atomic ground truth for this identity check."}
